key_sub: Torque = force × perpendicular distance from the pivot.
body_html:
How to think about it

Translational motion is motion along a line. Newton's laws explain it: an object keeps its motion unless a resultant force acts (inertia); F(net) = ma; and forces come in action–reaction pairs. Friction opposes motion and lets us walk and brake.

Rotational motion is turning about an axis. A force applied far from the pivot gives a large turning effect, or torque: τ = F × d. Objects balance when the clockwise and counterclockwise torques are equal. A low center of mass makes objects stable.

Example

A 60 kg cart accelerates at 2 m/s². Resultant force?

F = ma

Answer: 120 N

Example

Why is a door handle far from the hinges?

Torque = F × d

Answer: a larger distance gives more torque for the same force

Common mistakes

  • Thinking a moving object needs a force to keep moving.
  • Putting action and reaction forces on the same object.
  • Thinking torque depends only on force.

faq.a: Their bodies keep moving forward because of inertia.

faq.q: Why do tightrope walkers carry long poles?

items.q: A car moves along a straight road at a constant speed. Which statement is correct?

items.e: Balanced forces: constant velocity (or at rest). Unbalanced forces: acceleration in the direction of the resultant force.
